title: Industry and INL collaborate to test new varieties of TRISO fuel
summary: In the 1950s, nuclear scientists set out to design a different kind of nuclear fuel. Instead of relying primarily on reactor systems and large containment domes to prevent the release of radioactive material, researchers in the United States and Europe envisioned surrounding tiny uranium particles with their own miniature containment systems. Over the next 30 years, they developed the earliest tristructural isotropic (TRISO) fuel designs, covering particles with multiple containment layers and demonstrating that they could operate at very high temperatures while maintaining strong safety performance.

title: USDA opens nuclear power funding opportunity for rural electric cooperatives
summary: A new program from the U.S. Department of Agriculture has allocated $175 million for rural electric cooperatives to expand nuclear power and improve electricity transmission in rural communities. The new Affordable Rural Cooperative Program (ARC) will begin taking letters of interest from eligible applicants for the awards—which will be offered as loans and/or grants—beginning on October 19. The window closes on November 20.

title: MSRE FLiBe arrives in Texas for reuse after decades in storage
summary: This morning, more than 2 metric tons of FLiBe—a mixture of lithium fluoride and beryllium fluoride—was delivered to the Molten Salt Research Reactor (MSRR), a Natura Resources MSR-1, on the Abilene Christian University campus in Abilene, Texas. The shipment gives the salt a second life. It was originally used in the Molten Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which ceased operations in 1969. Since then, the salt has been stored with minimal use beyond the extraction of a small amount for research purposes.
